meiji_transition.summary: Tottori Prefecture was set up in 1871, merged into Shimane in 1876 and split off again in 1881.
meiji_transition.boundary_note: Tottori = Inaba (east) + Hōki (west); it was swallowed by Shimane for five years and re-established because people resented having their prefectural office far away in Matsue.

history_timeline.title: The White Hare of Inaba
history_timeline.summary: Setting of the Kojiki tale of the White Hare of Inaba; Ōtomo no Yakamochi, governor of Inaba, wrote the very last poem of the Man'yōshū here.

history_timeline.title: The emperor on Mount Senjō
history_timeline.summary: In 1333 Nawa Nagatoshi welcomed Emperor Go-Daigo, escaped from Oki, at Mount Senjō in Hōki and helped him overthrow the shogunate.

history_timeline.title: Yamana, 'lord of a sixth'
history_timeline.summary: The Yamana held Inaba, Hōki and other San'in provinces — at their height they were called 'Rokubun-no-ichi-dono', lords of a sixth of the realm.

history_timeline.title: The starvation of Tottori
history_timeline.summary: In 1581 Hideyoshi starved out Tottori Castle; its commander Kikkawa Tsuneie took his own life to spare the lives of his men and surrendered the castle.

history_timeline.title: Ikeda, 320,000 koku
history_timeline.summary: Ikeda Mitsunaka was given Tottori, and the Ikeda ruled Inaba and Hōki until the end of the Edo period.

history_timeline.title: Restored prefecture and dunes
history_timeline.summary: Tottori was restored in 1881; it is Japan's least populous prefecture, and the Tottori Sand Dunes and 'Kitarō Road' are its calling cards.

landmarks.name: Sanbutsu-ji Nageiredō
landmarks.note: A national-treasure hall perched on a cliff

specialties.name: Matsuba crab
specialties.note: Winter snow crab of the San'in coast

dialect.name: Tottori dialect
dialect.features: Inaba speech differs from Hōki speech (close to Izumo's); 'darazu' means fool, with endings like '-dakee'.

guide.opening: This old man is a kataribe of Izumo, a teller of ancient tales. This is where the White Hare met the god Ōkuninushi in the Kojiki — and later, where Hideyoshi starved a castle into surrender…

regional_meme.title: No Starbucks, but dunes
regional_meme.text: Tottori was once the only prefecture without a Starbucks; its governor quipped, 'We don't have Sutaba, but we have Sunaba (the sand pit)!'

regional_meme.title: Tottori or Shimane?
regional_meme.text: Outsiders can never remember which of Tottori and Shimane is on the left — the answer: Tottori is on the right (east).

hero_persona.name: Kikkawa Tsuneie
hero_persona.title: The commander who died to save his garrison
hero_persona.opening_line: I am Kikkawa Tsuneie. Tottori Castle was surrounded and its food ran out… I traded my life for the lives of thousands of my soldiers, and I do not regret it.
hero_persona.tone_prompt: solemn and quiet, with a strong sense of duty; grave when speaking of the siege

ramen.highlight: A rare beef-bone broth, sweet with the aroma of beef fat

sake.taste_profile: Rich & dry: brewed with Daisen spring water, best served warm
